pr_title: [Types] Fix entity-service's parameters inference for generic mapped types with deep literal intersections
pr_comments:
Although the fix is working in 99% of the use cases, when using an enum field (like `priceRange` in my example) alone in a filters object notation (nested or not), it leads to unwanted behavior (see image) with ObjectNotation not being inferred from usage.
![image](https://github.com/strapi/strapi/assets/25851739/bd270761-be22-43f5-a923-485f9f98f4cf)

I've spent way too much time and energy today trying to figure out where that particular issue is coming from. I'll continue tomorrow.

Managed to make a minimal reproduction example for whoever is interested

[Playground link](https://www.typescriptlang.org/play?#code/JYOwLgpgTgZghgYwgAgMoIBYQLZwM7IDeAUMsgORwAOwAdDAPYPkBcRyIc2EbeYUoAOYAaZBBABXbG3KNmyAD4UARnCjlRICHwgATNgCUICBlF0AePgJAjkEkAGsQDAO4gAfMgC+w0sgD0--GyANKArn-QHAtDJupszVfdritiahpkitatrtAuA3XEfWGpYARjYeKpyCmCVCZbiKGAeDw6zwom92AG6S0p3xCVKjud9ujYluyAA1MglVgHjB8ZzClAXQagtCwxGBFGY3HCYmm7UW9807TM9m-gCgRBZtG2rVtqR--BajqCTqCHMH5PADCQCVifjXvqqBGuQGAoAYRc9oipD4HxX7-uQQHgbvX1kFteAgcgXLsVglaIreqw4FAbIepi4S4rE9VKBoXYGHcT6kIACQYD00eNYQoF7XmACZhFoEXYgYHIIBQCc0e0PGQY+L6wiKOdSt3H1nvh6biBMEA+G5nNXN0Dzhh6hm5j2URCE4bgZHmLwFrsw0fvnPdXucbJVjVFAsUmFAYaVRIOISbW1T1vmDdAI3PNN2YmY0IgF1ti2OC4E5ZD2e3HaCJGEhVk7Xs9ldnulgASfkQ917IoAFiP3Ojs248t-k2HqQhE5UNRyC8dpM8VnO89dghC8nblS-5ecUQq0Jpf5LH3aXL2BmyaX-eyY5lIrsOAGZa6jk2G-mS3rbTw+BjpFu29uGRti7nuHcV521cXN2A+H4sx7pTeq4AFl342hhjozU+VtU5J2YKIZuyBW7ty2J3TQoCKB2zvlnKG5Nc4u3VkPZcI9fYTXml-NGABWP+9dY7AJgXbe+SEjBUASIgEoJowhZAwEaXsUNgBUm0LgqcM4UBpg+MJKGpgwhujPryBcgozxpFyq9f02hxAe2wcWamIl4rOSAA)

Well, so the issue here boils down to TypeScript's conditional and distributive behavior with union types. The union type (`TSchemaUID`) gets distributed across the types within `ObjectNotation`.

Instead of returning
```ts
AttributesFiltering<'api::a.a'> | AttributesFiltering<'api::b.b'> | ...
```
it's doing
```ts
AttributesFiltering<'api::a.a' | 'api::b.b' | ... >
```

under the hood

This distributive property of generics means that TypeScript has to keep every possibility open when building `ObjectNotation` (and thus `AttributesFiltering`), which essentially means that it leaves any `Common.UID.Schema` as open possibilities rather than narrowing it to one.

It seems that the reason it doesn't break when using non (literal) union types is because TypeScript needs more context or stricter type constraints to infer the exact type from the union. `enumeration` attributes' values are not considered as one type but as a union of multiple types and TS cannot guarantee which one is being inferred.

I managed to fix the faulty behavior by creating an intermediary mapping step for `TSchemaUID` in `ObjectNotation`. This allows TypeScript's generic inference to correctly distribute the `TSchemaUID` union into the individual keys of `AttributesFiltering` and `RootLevelOperatorFiltering` types.

In short, going from

```ts
export type ObjectNotation<TSchemaUID extends Common.UID.Schema> = RootLevelOperatorFiltering<TSchemaUID> & AttributesFiltering<TSchemaUID>;
```

to

```ts
export type ObjectNotation<TSchemaUID extends Common.UID.Schema> =
  TSchemaUID extends infer TUIDs extends Common.UID.Schema
    ? // The intermediary mapping step below allows TypeScript's generic inference to correctly distribute the
      // TSchemaUID union into the individual keys of AttributesFiltering and RootLevelOperatorFiltering types
      {
        [TUID in TUIDs]: RootLevelOperatorFiltering<TUID> & AttributesFiltering<TUID>;
      }[TSchemaUID]
    : never;
```

---

On a side note, now that we've implemented this intermediate step in `ObjectNotation`, we don't need any additional conditional statements within `AttributesFiltering` members.
Indeed, with the modification above, TypeScript will now correctly distribute the `TSchemaUID`. This essentially makes TypeScript check each key of the union individually ensuring that TS can infer the types correctly down the line.

~I haven't removed the conditionals from there though, as one could use those types directly without using the same distribution strategy as stated in `ObjectNotation`.~

EDIT: I've removed the conditionals as they were breaking the build (possibly causing an infinite recursion for non existing UIDs)

issue_context.title: Populate generated types doesn't work with filter on entityService
issue_context.body:
## Bug report

### Required System information

<!-- Please ensure you are using the Node LTS version (v16 or v18 or v20) -->
<!-- Strapi v3 is no longer supported, please update to Strapi v4 -->
<!-- If you are reporting a frontend bug please provide error logs after setting STRAPI_ENFORCE_SOURCEMAPS=true in your .env -->
<!-- This environment variable makes frontend errors easier to read and trace -->

- Node.js version: v16.20.0
- NPM version: 8.19.4
- Strapi version: 4.13.7
- Database: postfgres
- Operating system: wsl
- Is your project Javascript or Typescript: Typescript

### Describe the bug

I'm using entityService with the generated types, typing my strapi, and I note when a add a filter on my api, the populate fields type are gone from my types.

Before add filters (without error):
![image](https://github.com/strapi/strapi/assets/52859409/733f4462-7ad3-4ffa-b651-58372bd1cc4d)

On add filters (with type error):
![image](https://github.com/strapi/strapi/assets/52859409/3cd4b530-223d-472d-bfc5-214e6d33f9ad)

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. Creata a collection type with relation
2. Create a api with entityService without filters and populate and check the types
3. Add filters and check the types
4. See error

### Expected behavior

Don't gone my populated fields from types.

### Additional context

I don't know if is a bug or I'm using wrong, if anyone can help, thanks.
